# XERK-247: Add session and weekly limit status section to Turma Usage page

- URL: https://<INTERNAL_HOST>/browse/XERK-247
- Status: To Do
- Type: Story
- Priority: Medium
- Assignee: <REDACTED_NAME>
- Reporter: <REDACTED_NAME>
- Project: XerkTech (XERK)
- Labels: Turma

## Description

Goal

Surface Claude subscription session (5h) and weekly (7d) limit status directly on the Turma Usage page, so limit headroom is visible without opening Claude Settings.

Background

There is no public/official API for consumer subscription usage. Anthropic's documented Usage & Cost API and Analytics API require an Admin API key, are org-scoped, and are explicitly unavailable to individual accounts — and they report API token spend, not Pro/Max session and weekly caps.

Approach options

Option A — Claude Code statusLine hook (preferred, sanctioned)

Claude Code (v2.1.x+) passes rate_limits.five_hour and rate_limits.seven_day on stdin to the configured statusLine script for Pro/Max subscribers — used percentage plus reset timestamps, no network call.

- Configure statusLine to a wrapper script that both renders the normal status string and writes the raw JSON to a known path (or POSTs to a Turma ingest endpoint).
- Turma Usage page reads that snapshot and renders session/weekly bars with reset countdowns.
- Constraint: data only refreshes while a Claude Code session is active, and only after the first assistant message of that session. Snapshot must carry a timestamp so the UI can show staleness.

Option B — OAuth token fallback (unofficial, fragile)

Community statuslines call the usage endpoint directly using the OAuth token from ~/.claude/.credentials.json. Undocumented and unsupported; will break without notice, and aggressive polling returns rate_limit_error. Only consider as a gap-filler behind a feature flag.

Notes / gotchas

- The CLI's /usage numbers are computed from local sessions on that machine and exclude other devices and claude.ai, so they can trail the real server-side counter. Label the UI accordingly rather than presenting it as authoritative.
- Subscription usage is a single shared pool across claude.ai, Claude Code, and other Claude surfaces.
- Upstream feature request to watch: anthropics/claude-code#44328 (claude usage --json exposing session cap, weekly cap, and extra usage balance). If shipped, it replaces both options above.

Acceptance criteria

- Usage page shows session (5h) and weekly (7d) percentage used with reset countdowns.
- Stale data is visibly marked with a last-updated timestamp.
- No credentials or tokens are embedded in Turma; ingest path is read-only from a local snapshot.
- Graceful empty state when no snapshot exists (e.g. no Claude Code session has run).

QA branch `XERK-252` in the Turma repo at <INTERNAL_PATH> (one commit, 05ceb86, on top of origin/main which now contains the merged XERK-251). Read `qa.md` first — you updated it last run, and §3.1 (fake tunnel-agent) plus §2.5 (Android in the agent image) are exactly what this needs.

BACKGROUND: this fixes the pre-existing defect your last run found and recorded in qa.md §6.2 — "an agent tunnel flap permanently kills an open chat's live stream". Jira XERK-252. Diagnosis: the hub is fine (it holds the browser's `/live` socket across a control-channel flap and re-arms the agent's watch on reconnect); `turma/public/sessions.html`'s `render()` vanish check was treating `terminalOnline === false` as the session having vanished and calling `clearStage()`. Production logs show this is routine, not exotic: every hub restart flaps all six hosts' tunnels at once (6/6 reconnects in the same second, twice on 11 Aug), so every deploy evicted every operator mid-read.

THE CHANGE:
- `render()` now clears the stage only on positive evidence about the SESSION: `sessionRecord(currentId)` (whole fleet, unfiltered) + `agentByKey(currentHostKey)`. Clear iff the host is reporting AND (no record OR `status !== "running"`). Hold when the host is absent from the payload, and hold when its tunnel is merely down.
- Reading the unfiltered fleet also means narrowing the header's org filter no longer closes the staged session (XERK-62 says scoping is a sidebar concern).
- `setStageTunnel(online)` paints a `⚠ tunnel offline` chip in both the chat and terminal bars, and on the false→true TRANSITION only: calls `TurmaChat.reconnectNow()` and, in terminal view, re-navigates the ttyd iframe.
- `chat.js`: new `reconnectNow()` (no-op when the socket is OPEN/CONNECTING or no session; else clears the retry timer, resets backoff, reopens). `loadHistory()` bails before building its URL when gen is stale or the ids are null (kills the `/api/agents/null/sessions/null/history` 404).
- `android/`: `ChatUiState.tunnelOnline` off the fleet heartbeat, rendered in the chat header ("⚠ tunnel offline" outranking "· live", because our own socket stays open across a flap).
- Vendored `chat.cjs` re-copied to glasses + veiller; `.claude/rules/turma.md` documents the rule.

CLAIMS TO FALSIFY — please attack each in a real browser against a real hub, not from the diff:
1. Dropping the agent's `/agent/control` channel while a chat is open no longer clears the stage: the conversation stays on screen, the chip appears, and when the fake agent reconnects the live stream RESUMES ON ITS OWN (new `{turn}`/`{tail}` frames render) without the operator touching anything. This is the exact scenario you reproduced last run — re-run your old script and confirm it now recovers.
2. Same for the terminal view: the ttyd iframe is re-navigated on tunnel return (transition only — a steady stream of online beats must not re-navigate, which would restart the terminal every few seconds).
3. A session that genuinely goes (killed elsewhere → host reports it stopped or drops it from `sessions`) STILL clears the stage. This must not regress into a stage that never lets go.
4. A payload that omits the host entirely (hub restarted before the first heartbeat, failed refresh, `agents: []`) holds the stage rather than clearing.
5. Narrowing the org filter while a session is staged keeps it on the stage.
6. No `/api/agents/null/...` request is ever issued after a stage is cleared (watch the hub's access log / your CDP network capture).
7. Nothing else on the Sessions page regressed — selection, kill/rename/move menus, ended-session views, deep links (`?session=`, `?spawn=`, `?ended=`), the compose draft carry, verbosity, terminal toggle.

Also please probe for what I might have got wrong rather than only confirming: e.g. does the stage now hold a session whose HOST went away for good (agent machine off) in a way that misleads — can the operator still tell, and can they still leave? Does `currentHostKey` go stale after a session is migrated to another host (XERK-101) or after a resume under a new id? Is there any path where `reconnectNow()` fires against a session that is no longer the staged one?
